argv: want=$(sed -n "s/^go //p" go.mod); have=$(go env GOVERSION) || exit 127; [ "$have" = "go$want" ] || { echo "$have found; go.mod needs go$want" >&2; exit 1; }

p=$(command -v ocr) || { echo "open-code-review (ocr) is not installed" >&2; exit 127; }; case "$p" in /*) ;; *) p="$(pwd)/$p" ;; esac; "$p" delegate preview --help >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "$p has no delegation mode; install open-code-review 1.9 or later" >&2; exit 1; }; printf '%s\n' "$p"

c="${GRAPHLOOM_CODEX_BIN:-codex}"; h="${GRAPHLOOM_CODEX_HOME:-${CODEX_HOME:-}}"; [ -z "$h" ] || export CODEX_HOME="$h"; "$c" --version >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Codex ($c) is not installed" >&2; exit 127; }; "$c" login status >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Codex is not logged in${h:+ for $h}: run $c login" >&2; exit 1; }

c="${GRAPHLOOM_CLAUDE_BIN:-claude}"; d="${GRAPHLOOM_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-}}"; [ -z "$d" ] || export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="$d"; "$c" --version >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Claude Code ($c) is not installed" >&2; exit 127; }; "$c" auth status >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Claude Code is not logged in${d:+ for $d}: run $c auth login" >&2; exit 1; }
make --version 2>/dev/null | grep -q "GNU Make" || { echo "GNU make required" >&2; exit 1; }

v=$(node --version 2>/dev/null) || { echo "Node.js >= 24.6.0 is required (make generate and make build run npm ci for the ui and mcp projects, on every task)" >&2; exit 127; }; n=$(echo "$v" | sed -n "s/^v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\).*/\1 \2/p"); set -- $n; maj=${1:-0}; min=${2:-0}; { [ "$maj" -gt 24 ] || { [ "$maj" -eq 24 ] && [ "$min" -ge 6 ]; }; } || { echo "Node.js >= 24.6.0 required, found $v" >&2; exit 1; }

want=" banyand/metadata/metadata.go banyand/metadata/schema/schema.go banyand/queue/queue.go pkg/flow/types.go pkg/meter/meter.go pkg/node/interface.go "; bad=""; for f in $(grep -rl "go:generate" --include="*.go" api banyand bydbctl fodc pkg 2>/dev/null | sort); do case "$want" in *" $f "*) ;; *) bad="$bad $f";; esac; done; [ -z "$bad" ] || { echo "go:generate directives in files the generate-mocks inputs do not cover:$bad; update this profile" >&2; exit 1; }
make -C banyand generate && make -C pkg generate

pkgs=$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=d HEAD~1 HEAD -- "*.go" | while read -r f; do d=$(dirname "$f"); [ -d "$d" ] && echo "./$d"; done | sort -u | tr "\n" " "); [ -n "$pkgs" ] || { echo "the change touches no Go package" >&2; exit 1; }; exec make test-ci PKG="$pkgs"
commands.statement: make test-ci passes for the changed Go packages

commands.label: make check (which includes license-check and check-format)

planning.reach: Reach: for every behaviour the fix changes, the basis of that decision names each caller and lifecycle path that depends on the old behaviour (shutdown and Close, context cancellation, error returns, panics, retries, concurrency, resource release), starting with the changed type's own Close, Stop and shutdown paths, and the test that covers it; a path no test covers is stated there as a risk. For a wait the fix makes longer or unbounded, say what happens when the awaited code ignores cancellation or never returns.

implementation.conventions: Use run.Go rather than raw goroutines, and follow the repository's conventions.
implementation.checks: The controller checks your change in clean checkouts: the base commit with only your test files must fail the test by assertion; the full change must pass the test, `make test-ci` for the changed packages, and make lint, build and check (`make check` includes license-check and check-format). The cheap checks (the test, `make test-ci` and `make lint`) run first and the build and check only when they pass. `make check` must leave no file changed, so run `make format` if you touch Go code.
selfCheck: go vet $(git ls-files -m -o --exclude-standard -- '*.go' | xargs -r -n1 dirname | sort -u | sed 's|^|./|')
golangci-lint run $(git ls-files -m -o --exclude-standard -- '*.go' | xargs -r -n1 dirname | sort -u | sed 's|^|./|')
implementation.cleanCheckHint: make check reformats Go code; run make format

rules: Beyond the diff's own correctness, review what the change breaks.

For every behaviour the change alters, search for each caller and lifecycle path that depends on the old behaviour: shutdown and Close, context cancellation, error returns, panics, retries, concurrency and resource release.

Report at high severity: a path whose behaviour changes without a test in this change covering it; a removed guarantee (a bound, a timeout, a cleanup, a cancellation) that other code or comments still rely on; a comment that describes a guarantee the change removed; a test whose expected value is derived from the new code rather than from the issue; a change to an on-disk or wire format.
Report at medium severity a goroutine started without run.Go or the package's existing lifecycle helper.

checklist: - [x] Add a unit test to verify that the fix works.
- [x] Explain briefly why the bug exists and how to fix it.
footer: - [x] If this pull request closes/resolves/fixes an existing issue, replace the issue number. Fixes {issue}.
pullRequest.e2eNote: The end-to-end tests (Kind) were not run; this change needs them.
